# ProveIt research package — 8 October 2026

Three substantial articles, prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov with OpenAI ChatGPT. The package contains **59 pages of mathematical manuscripts**, complete LaTeX sources, exact verification programs, numerical diagnostics where relevant, source audits, and proposed research agendas.

## Articles

| Directory | Article | Pages | Main contribution |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 01_universal_avoidance | A common avoiding set for stable recurrences and balanced P-recursive sequences | 23 | One near-full-measure set simultaneously avoids every nontrivial affine copy of every sequence in the stated recurrence class, with infinitely many omissions. |
| 02_parabolic_amplitudes | A Common Density for Parabolic Iteration | 16 | Exact Bell–Euler amplitude identification, positive-axis analyticity, justified geometric depth summation, and weighted partition-chain constants. |
| 03_tree_broadcast | A sharp analytic renormalization threshold for binary broadcasts on trees | 20 | The exact threshold theta>b^(-3/4), analytic critical-window residues, arbitrary-order local expansions, and majority-decoding corrections. |

Each directory contains article.tex and article.pdf, a README, verification code and results, and pinned provenance. The first article uses four additional numbered TeX files and one generated figure. The other articles are standalone TeX sources.

## Principal results

### 1. Universal recurrence avoidance

For every epsilon in (0,1), one closed symmetric 1-periodic set F has measure greater than 1-epsilon in every unit interval and omits infinitely many terms from every nonzero affine copy of every real sequence satisfying:

- It is not eventually zero.
- It decays exponentially.
- Eventually it satisfies a polynomial recurrence whose first and last coefficient polynomials have the common maximal degree.

The same F works for all such sequences and all orders and real parameters. In particular, it covers every stable constant-coefficient recurrence, including complex characteristic roots, repeated roots, exact cancellations, and infinitely many zero terms. Convergent C-finite sequences are covered after subtracting their limit, provided they are not eventually constant.

The proof selects nonzero coordinates of successive small recurrence states, then uses polynomial sign conditions to make finite routing uniform over the continuum of parameters. Countable compact exhaustion handles all balanced recurrences. The effective version gives an effectively closed set with computable measure; a practical blocker-construction program is not claimed.

### 2. A common parabolic density

For f(z)=exp(z)-1 and H(n,m)=n![z^n]f^m(z), let h be the positive Laplace density of the normalized entire Fatou orbit and I the existing compact-ratio Bell amplitude. The paper proves

    I(t) = t 2^(t/3) h(t),  t>0,

and consequently continues h holomorphically to Re t>0. It constructs finite positive coefficient measures whose Laplace limit identifies h and whose local coefficient limit identifies I. This fixes the normalization without comparing global contours.

The global-depth estimate is

    sum_m exp(-Lm) H(n,m)
      ~ (n!)^2 (2L)^(-n) n^(-1-L/3) L^(L/3-1) I(L).

It is uniform on positive compact L-intervals. For strict chains marked by q, L(q)=log(1+1/q), the identified amplitude is

    C(q) = (2L(q))^(L(q)/3) h(L(q))/(q+1).

This C extends holomorphically to Re q>0. At q=1 the formula identifies the existing Lengyel constant. Classical leading chain asymptotics are credited; their mere existence is not claimed as new.

The main implication explicitly imports four analytic statements from the pinned, unrefereed ProveIt Euler/Bell reports. Endpoint and chain-length corollaries state their additional source dependencies.

### 3. Tree-broadcast analytic threshold

For a rooted b-ary binary broadcast with fixed positive root, independent edge signs of mean theta, and level sum S_n, put X_n=(b theta)^(-n)S_n. The transforms

    exp(-Var(X_n) t^2/2) E exp(t X_n)

converge locally holomorphically near zero if and only if theta>b^(-3/4), for 0<theta<=1. The residue is jointly analytic in theta and t and convergence is exponential on compact parameter intervals.

The parity decomposition of the logarithm is decisive. Its odd part has contraction multiplier (b theta)^(-2); the remaining even part starts at degree four and has multiplier b/(b theta)^4. Explicit third- and fourth-cumulant divergences prove the converse, including the boundary.

The paper then proves all-order expansions in the depth window theta_n=b^(-1/2)exp(gamma/(2n)), full lattice local asymptotics, and an independent Fourier formula for majority success. At exact criticality on the binary tree,

    p_n = 1/2 + 1/sqrt(pi n) - 5/(4 sqrt(pi) n^(5/2)) + O(n^(-7/2)).

The n^(-3/2) term vanishes. Removing sufficiently many even cumulants also gives analytic renormalization for every theta>1/b.

## Proof and novelty status

These are research manuscripts with complete arguments for the new claims, not declarations of external peer review or worldwide priority. THEOREM_LEDGER.json records the statements and dependencies. REVIEW_NOTES.md records the internal mathematical checks and concrete limitations.

The avoidance routing method is inherited and reproved. The tree paper is self-contained and does not assume the factor-of-IID theorem that motivated its selection. The parabolic paper is an explicit implication from four named analytic interfaces in earlier unrefereed reports. None of the manuscripts is proof-assistant verified.

The papers identify genuine extensions or unresolved questions in the inspected snapshots. Their eventual assessment as breakthroughs, and priority relative to the entire literature, requires specialist review. Numerical agreement is never used as a proof of an analytic theorem.

## Reproduce

Required:

- Python 3.10 or later.
- SymPy for the parabolic exact coordinate check.
- TeX Live with latexmk and the standard packages loaded by the sources.

Optional:

- mpmath for the parabolic numerical diagnostics.
- Matplotlib for regenerating the signed-sampling illustration.

The requirements.txt file lists the Python packages. All verification programs are offline. From this top-level directory:

```sh
python3 reproduce.py --checks
python3 reproduce.py --pdfs
```

Running both options performs both actions. The commands overwrite only the recorded verification outputs and TeX build products. Optional numerical and figure commands appear in the individual READMEs. Their stored results and the figure are already included.

The exact suites were executed during preparation and all passed. A total scalar-check count across papers would obscure the different experiments; the reports retain their separate scopes:

| Article | Selected exact checks |
|---|---|
| Avoidance | 168 independent recurrence terms; 896 matrix-product terms; 2,184 sign comparisons; 51 boundary triples; 24 window cases; 65,536 routing event cases |
| Parabolic | 960 coefficient majorants; 144 Newton-basis evaluations; 96 rational geometric mixtures; Fatou defect through degree five |
| Tree broadcast | 392 exact scalar checks plus fixed-series checks through degree ten, with independent finite generating functions |

The parabolic inverse-Laplace runs are exploratory, not interval-certified. They agree to at least twelve decimal places at the four displayed arguments. The exact and numerical roles are distinguished in the article and receipts.

All three final PDFs were compiled and rendered for visual inspection. The final compilation logs had no warnings, undefined references, overfull boxes, or underfull boxes.

## Suggested integration

INTEGRATION_MAP.json gives suggested destinations. These are proposed locations for review, not a record of a committed repository change.

- Place the avoidance directory alongside the earlier uniform-geometric-avoidance report.
- Place the parabolic directory alongside the Euler, Bell, and strict-chain reports, and link the resolved question labels from those reports.
- Place the tree paper in a probability/tree-broadcast research directory; the suggested new path can be adapted to the repository's preferred taxonomy.

Retain entire article directories so that all relative TeX, code, data, and figure paths work. An editor can add cross-references to existing reports without altering the proved statements. Source pins preserve the baseline for each comparison.

The repository snapshots used were:

- openai/math: adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a
- VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt: 58175ca45563d9ee29875374dd77942f069268a9

## Further research

The three articles contain 26 proposed research directions, each with motivation and a stated boundary. RESEARCH_QUESTIONS.json provides a selected machine-readable list for issue creation. Especially concrete next steps are:

1. Extend signed sampling to polynomially growing inverse-state norms.
2. Obtain usable size bounds or verified finite certificates for recurrence blockers.
3. Determine what parameter-complexity growth can replace the present subexponential condition.
4. Prove a Bell coefficient theorem uniform as n/m tends to zero and justify all-order depth summation.
5. Investigate complex zero-freeness and global marked-chain asymptotics.
6. Certify the common density and its derivatives numerically.
7. Determine the maximal complex domain and sharp convergence rates of the tree residue.
8. Classify higher even-cumulant thresholds and possible cancellations.
9. Compare majority with the full posterior in the finite-depth critical window.

These are proposed targets; the package does not certify that every formulation is absent from the wider literature.

## Attribution and integrity

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt and third_party/ retain attribution and license information for the inherited OpenAI routing construction. Original repository articles are linked by immutable source references rather than duplicated in full. Each article credits the primary literature it uses.

SHA256SUMS records the bytes in this package before compression. The PDFs are readable deliverables; the TeX and scripts are the editable and reproducible sources.

For each $\varepsilon>0$ we construct one closed, symmetric, $1$-periodic set of measure greater than $1-\varepsilon$ per period that simultaneously avoids every nontrivial affine copy of every non-eventually-zero, exponentially decaying real sequence satisfying a polynomial-coefficient linear recurrence whose first and last coefficients have the common maximal degree. Every affine pattern has infinitely many terms outside the set. In particular, the same set works for all stable constant-coefficient recurrences, with arbitrary orders, complex characteristic roots, repeated roots, exact zeros, and real initial values. It also works for balanced hypergeometric sequences and exponentially damped Legendre sequences.

The new sampling argument uses the maximum of a finite recurrence state. Invertibility prevents a whole state from collapsing between successive steps, even when individual coordinates oscillate or vanish. A polynomial sign-condition count then makes the finite routing construction uniform over uncountably many parameters. We give a complete proof of the routing and repair argument, crediting its geometric antecedents. An effective compactness argument supplies finite rational certificates and an effectively closed common set with computable measure. The full construction is an existence algorithm with very large cost; the accompanying exact programs check the local identities, not a practical instance of the universal set. The general Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture remains outside the result.

Two recent ProveIt reports study different arrays governed by the same
parabolic map $f(z)=e^z-1$. One constructs a positive density $h$ whose
Laplace transform is the normalized entire Fatou orbit $P$; the other
obtains an iterated-Bell amplitude $I$ from a fixed contour.
Their precise relation was left as an explicit open question. We prove
\[
 I(t)=t\,2^{t/3}h(t)\qquad(t>0)
\]
by identifying two limits of positive coefficient measures. This avoids
a global comparison of the two contours and proves that $h$ extends
holomorphically to $\Re t>0$. A coefficientwise rational majorant then
controls every iteration depth in a geometric aggregate. It gives the
exact Lengyel-constant identity and, more generally, a holomorphic
formula on $\Re q>0$ for the leading amplitude of strict partition chains
marked by $q$. Complete proofs, source pins, exact finite checks and
independent numerical diagnostics are supplied. The analytic inputs
from the earlier reports are identified explicitly; no worldwide
priority claim or new leading-equivalent claim is made.

Let $S_n$ be the sum of the spins at level $n$ of a rooted $b$-ary
binary broadcast, with the root fixed to $+1$ and edge correlation
$0<\theta\leq1$. Put $X_n=(b\theta)^{-n}S_n$. We prove that the
Gaussian-renormalized Laplace transforms
$\exp(-\Var(X_n)t^2/2)\E e^{tX_n}$ converge locally holomorphically
near zero if and only if $\theta>b^{-3/4}$. The limiting residue is
nonvanishing and depends analytically on $\theta$; convergence is
exponential, uniformly on compact parameter intervals above the threshold.
The converse follows from explicit third- and fourth-cumulant divergences,
including the boundary case. This fourth-cumulant threshold is distinct
from the classical reconstruction threshold $b^{-1/2}$.

For the finite-depth window
$\theta_n=b^{-1/2}\exp(\gamma/(2n))$, we identify a single analytic
residue controlling all bounded real $\gamma$, obtain expansions to
every order in $n^{-1}$, and prove a uniform lattice local limit expansion
to arbitrary order. A separate Fourier argument gives the full expansion
of majority-decoding success. On the binary tree at criticality its
$n^{-3/2}$ correction vanishes, and the next term is
$-5/(4\sqrt\pi\,n^{5/2})$. The proofs use exact broadcast recursions,
analytic contractions, and conditional independence; no factor-of-IID
claim is assumed. Exact rational computations verify the coefficient
identities and independent finite probability distributions. The classical
central limit theorem and earlier moment recursions are credited; the
precise novelty of the stronger theorem package remains subject to
specialist literature review.

# Recurrence avoidance and optimal simplex products

Research package prepared for the ProveIt project, 8 October 2026.

This archive contains two independent mathematical manuscripts, their complete
LaTeX sources, compiled PDFs, exact verification programs, recorded results,
and source-audit information. The papers do not depend on each other's results.
The outer archive is a delivery bundle containing two manuscripts; for the
repository's one-manuscript-per-intake-archive convention, treat the two
manuscript directories as separate sources and retain their shared preamble.

| Manuscript | PDF | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Large Closed Sets Avoiding All Convergent Linear Recurrences** | [recurrence_avoidance.pdf](recurrence_avoidance/recurrence_avoidance.pdf) | [main.tex](recurrence_avoidance/main.tex), with `sections/` and `references.tex` |
| **Optimal simplex products for projection-body volume** | [optimal_simplex_products.pdf](simplex_products/optimal_simplex_products.pdf) | [main.tex](simplex_products/main.tex) and [body.tex](simplex_products/body.tex) |

Both manuscripts use [common/preamble.tex](common/preamble.tex). Keep this
directory beside the two manuscript directories when rebuilding the package.
The delivered [BUILD_INFO.json](BUILD_INFO.json) records the compilation
environment and PDF inspection. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the delivery hashes;
from the extracted package root, check it with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`.
Follow the repository's intake convention for dropping delivery checksum
manifests after verification.

## 1. Main result: one large closed set for all convergent recurrences

For every real `0 < epsilon < 1`, the main paper constructs a closed, symmetric,
one-periodic set `F_epsilon` whose measure in every unit interval is at least
`1 - epsilon/2`, hence greater than `1 - epsilon`. This **one set works
simultaneously** for every convergent, non-eventually-constant real C-finite
sequence: every translation and nonzero dilation of such a sequence has
infinitely many terms outside `F_epsilon`.

Here C-finite means that a homogeneous linear recurrence with constant real
coefficients holds, possibly only from some index onward. The order, real
coefficients, and initial data are unrestricted. Negative and nonreal roots,
repeated roots, spectral collisions, and infinitely many zero terms are
allowed. The eventual-constancy exclusion and the nonzero-dilation condition
are necessary.

The same set also handles every non-eventually-constant **rational observation
of finitely many convergent C-finite sequences**, when the rational function's
denominator does not vanish at the limiting vector. Its basic quotient theorem
applies to `a_n/b_n` when `a_n -> 0` is not eventually zero and
`b_n -> b_infinity != 0`, with both numerator and denominator C-finite.

Examples include damped rotations, polynomial factors from repeated roots,
observations of stable matrix orbits, and `q^n/(1+q^n)` for `0 < q < 1`.
The new sampling argument controls a quadratic norm of a consecutive-state
block, then chooses an actual scalar term from that block. It therefore does
not require scalar terms to be positive or their consecutive ratios to exist.

### Effective construction: theorem versus implementation

For rational `epsilon`, the proof gives an effectively closed compact section
`F_epsilon intersect [0,1]` with computable measure. A proved terminating search
enumerates finite rational open-arc blockers and checks their uniform hitting
property, including a positive hitting margin, by real quantifier elimination.

**That full quantifier-elimination search and the ordered random routing
construction are not implemented in this package.** The executable verifier
checks finite-dimensional algebra, sampling, indexing, and boundary cases in
three explicit examples. It is not a program that outputs the universal set.
The proof supplies no practical complexity bound for producing its blockers.

The theorem does not cover every quotient with a vanishing limiting
denominator, arbitrary variable-coefficient recurrences, arbitrary analytic
observations, or all infinite subsets of the line. The paper also proves an
elementary limitation: allowing every perturbation `q^n + o(q^n)` is already
too broad for one positive-measure set to avoid all affine copies. This is not
a claimed solution of the full Erdős similarity conjecture.

## 2. Companion result: exact optimization of simplex products

For a convex body `K` in dimension `n`, let

`R_n(K) = volume(Pi K) / volume(K)^(n-1)`.

The companion determines its maximum over affine images of Cartesian products
of simplices. With `s_d = (d+1)d^d/d!`, the problem becomes maximizing
`product(s_(d_i))` over all positive factor dimensions summing to `n`.

The paper proves the following exact results.

- **Dimension 13 is the unique optimal exponential block size:**
  `sup_d s_d^(1/d) = s_13^(1/13)`, approximately `2.80996473256`.
- **Every dimension requires only two candidates.** Their factor counts are
  `max(1, floor(n/13))` and `ceil(n/13)`; each candidate has balanced factor
  dimensions.
- **From dimension 100 onward, the optimum has an exact rule modulo 13.**
  If `r = n mod 13` is at most 8, use `r` factors of dimension 14 and fill the
  remaining dimension with factors of dimension 13. If `r` is at least 9, use
  `13-r` factors of dimension 12 and fill the rest with dimension 13.
- **In every dimension at least 100, the maximizing dimension multiset is
  unique**, and every other multiset loses at least the sharp multiplicative factor
  `G = s_14^8/(s_13^4 s_12^5)`, approximately `1.00103981380358`.
- The optimum satisfies the exact recurrence `P_(n+13) = s_13 P_n` for
  `n >= 100`, has a fully determined periodic asymptotic expansion relative
  to a simplex, and admits exact optimization at prescribed factor or facet
  count. The threshold 100 and the uniform gap are both sharp.

The geometric identities are re-proved, with attribution to the inspected
source. The new contribution is the optimization of the product class. The
paper does not determine the maximum over arbitrary convex bodies. Arbitrary
simplex shapes in the same dimensions are affinely equivalent, so its
uniqueness and gap statements refer to dimension multisets or their affine
product classes.

## 3. Rebuild the PDFs

Requirements are a modern TeX installation with pdfLaTeX and the packages in
`common/preamble.tex`, plus GNU Make and a POSIX shell for the supplied Makefile.
The package was built with pdfTeX from TeX Live 2023. The included figures mean
that no Python plotting packages are required merely to rebuild the PDFs.

From this package directory:

```sh
make pdfs
```

Each article is compiled three times to stabilize references and the table of
contents. The output paths are the PDF paths listed above. To force rebuilding
existing PDFs, use `make -B pdfs`. The default `make` target also builds both
PDFs. Bibliographies are included in the LaTeX sources; BibTeX is not required.
Use `make recurrence` or `make simplex` to build only one article.

The equivalent per-paper command, run in its manuscript directory, is:

```sh
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -jobname=recurrence_avoidance main.tex
```

or, for the companion:

```sh
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -jobname=optimal_simplex_products main.tex
```

Repeat the relevant command until cross-references stabilize. On Windows, the
Makefile can be used in WSL or another compatible POSIX environment; the
per-paper commands also work from an appropriately configured terminal.
PDF byte hashes can change with TeX versions and build metadata even when the
mathematical content and layout agree.

`make clean` removes only generated TeX auxiliary files for these two job
names. It preserves the PDFs, sources, figures, recorded evidence, and any
delivery checksum manifest.

## 4. Reproduce the exact checks

Python 3.10 or newer is sufficient; the verification programs use only the
standard library. The recorded environment used Python 3.12.14. All
mathematical comparisons in the verifiers use exact rational arithmetic.

```sh
make verify
```

The Makefile copies the verification programs into `build/verification/`, runs
those copies, and compares the new evidence with the delivered records. It
does not overwrite the delivered evidence. Override the interpreter or the
reproduction directory if needed:

```sh
make verify PYTHON=python VERIFY_DIR=/tmp/proveit_research_checks
```

| Check | Recorded scope | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Recurrence sampling and rational normalization | Three explicit examples, 3,380 exact assertions, including 16 threshold-equality witnesses | `recurrence_avoidance/verification/results.json` |
| Simplex-product arithmetic and optimization | Seven strict rational enclosures, eight initial comparisons, prime-power identities, and an exact dynamic program through dimension 300 | `simplex_products/verification/results/` |
| Independently implemented simplex optimum and runner-up calculation | Exact best and runner-up values and all maximizing multisets through dimension 260 | `simplex_products/verification/results/independent_audit_report.json` |

The assertion count describes the finite run; it is not evidence for an
uncountable-parameter theorem by extrapolation. The recurrence proof rests on
the sign-condition bound, the finite conditional-probability argument,
compactness, and the summable construction. The simplex proofs establish the
classification in every dimension by concavity and deficit bounds, with
finite exact inequalities for the constants. The dynamic programs check the
formulas and implementations independently on their stated ranges.

The three verification targets can also be run separately:

```sh
make verify-recurrence
make verify-simplex
make verify-independent
```

### Optional figure regeneration

The recurrence paper includes the source for its two scientific figures:

```sh
make figures
```

This runs `python3 recurrence_avoidance/figures/generate_figures.py` by default;
the `PYTHON` Make variable selects a different interpreter.

This optional step requires NumPy and Matplotlib; the recorded environment
used NumPy 2.3.5 and Matplotlib 3.10.8. It rewrites the two figure pairs in
`recurrence_avoidance/figures/`, so run it on a working copy when preserving
delivered hashes. The displayed values come from the exact verifier; only
rendering uses floating-point values.

## 5. Provenance, claim status, and proposed ProveIt integration

[SOURCE_AUDIT.md](SOURCE_AUDIT.md) records the pinned repository snapshots,
the inherited ingredients, the present extensions, and the limits of the
literature and proof reviews. The source comparison uses:

- `openai/math` at `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`;
- `VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt` at `58175ca45563d9ee29875374dd77942f069268a9`.

The older ProveIt revision recorded inside the predecessor's own audit belongs
to that predecessor's provenance; it is not the snapshot for this delivery.
The manuscripts distinguish results inherited from those sources from the
new extensions proved here. Priority is assessed against inspected sources
and targeted literature searches, not certified globally. The package does
not claim external peer review or Lean/Rocq formal verification.

For intake, treat the two manuscripts as distinct reports:

| Paper | Proposed placement or continuation |
|---|---|
| Recurrence avoidance | Continue `Analysis/ErdosSimilarity/Research/uniform-geometric-avoidance/`, following the repository's procedure for a new source that extends an existing report. A separate `uniform-recurrence-avoidance` report beside it is another possible maintainer choice. |
| Simplex products | A new convex-geometry report in the research-report collection; a proposed destination is `SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/convex-geometry/optimal-simplex-products/`. The category and final path should be checked against the current catalogue at intake. |

Keep the delivered structure intact during review. If the papers are placed
separately, preserve the shared preamble dependency or adjust their input paths
as part of integration. The verification programs, their recorded outputs,
and the source audit belong with their respective report. Follow the
repository's current rules for delivery checksums and cataloguing.

These paths are integration proposals. This delivery does not represent a
repository push, merge, or modification of the existing ProveIt reports.

# Reciprocal-gamma kernels in the Stieltjes derivative tower

**Research article, proposed corrections, exact certificates, and reproducibility tools.**
Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt project on 2026-10-07.

Start with `article/stieltjes-zero-geometry-and-regularized-jets.pdf` (22 pages).
The complete LaTeX source and three table inputs are in the same directory.

## Results and their status

Write `gamma_n^(k)(a)` for the k-th derivative in the Hurwitz parameter a of
 the n-th generalized Stieltjes constant. Throughout, a > 0 and k >= 1.

1. **Analytic theorem:** there are at most n positive zeros, counting
   multiplicity, for every n and k. The proof uses a common Laplace kernel,
   the simple real roots of reciprocal-gamma Appell polynomials, and a
   multiplicity-sensitive variation argument proved in the article.
2. **Analytic theorem:** for fixed n, exactly n simple positive zeros exist
   for all sufficiently large k. Their slopes and the next two asymptotic
   coefficients are explicit, and a justified all-orders recursion is given.
   No uniformity for growing n is claimed.
3. **Analytic propagation theorem + finite exact certificates:** saturation
   at one k persists forever with strict right-interlacing. Fourteen exact
   sign enclosures establish the initial case k=1 for n=1,2,3,4. Thus these
   indices have exactly n simple zeros for every k >= 1.
4. **Entirely analytic first-index theorem:** the unique zero alpha_k obeys
   `exp(H_(k-1)) < alpha_k < exp(H_(k-1)) + 1/2`. Its location has a three-term
   expansion `exp(EulerGamma)*k + d + c/(k+1) + O(k^(-2))`, with d and c
   explicit in the article. Eight width-10^(-20) intervals are certified.
5. **Analytic arithmetic identities:** regularized Dirichlet L-jets across
   trivial zeros are transported by two parity-dependent kernels. Combining
   transport with the derivative tower cancels all conductor and harmonic
   factors from the kernel. The first bridge at a trivial zero contains
   `L''(-k)/(2*L'(-k))`, with conjugation for nonreal characters.

These are research claims supported by the included proofs. They have not been
independently refereed or formalized in Lean. Priority is not established by the
limited literature check. The classical parameter-derivative identity is
credited to prior work, not claimed as a new theorem. No special-value linear
or algebraic independence is claimed.

## What was audited

The main source is
`Analysis/Polylogarithms/docs/articles/stieltjes-parameter-derivative-tower.tex`
at commit `c78c7c3dc2fc742a1af9492e47d578b3fb4e01e7`, blob
`e4d53b7c921c72ff40c5393a9d3ac5cfb44ea6bb`.
The introductory antiderivative calculus and CM row-sum article were consulted
for context. This is **not** a full audit of the directory or a recertification
of every displayed table.

The four proposed changes in `corrections/` distinguish an unsupported
independence inference, a missing general rank proof, an underspecified
trivial-zero normalization, and an inaccurately described residual vocabulary.
No counterexample to the rank formula is asserted. No repository file was changed.

## Reproduce

Python 3.10 or later is required. Exact verification needs only its standard
library. Optional symbolic and numerical checks use SymPy and mpmath:

```sh
python tools/exact_verify.py
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python tools/symbolic_checks.py
python tools/numerical_checks.py
```

The delivered run passed **30 exact sign certificates**, **80 symbolic
regression checks**, and **48 high-precision regression checks**. The numerical
script also computed nine first-index roots. Numerical computations do not
replace the exact sign certificates or the analytic proofs.

`data/certificates.json` is the exact verifier's input. Each output enclosure
is obtained afresh, not trusted from a stored answer. The exact verifier uses
outward integer intervals at scale 10^90, a rational atanh-series logarithm with
an explicit tail, exact Bernoulli numbers, and the article's proved
Euler--Maclaurin remainder. A certificate is accepted only when its entire
interval has the requested strict sign. An inconclusive interval causes a
failure, not a claim that the sign is zero.

The fixed default working precision is sufficient for the supplied certificates;
the theoretical general threshold-search principle is not implemented as a
production search program. Computational complexity of that search is not claimed.

Build the article with a standard TeX Live installation:

```sh
cd article
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error \
  stieltjes-zero-geometry-and-regularized-jets.tex
```

Alternatively use `make exact`, `make symbolic`, `make numerical`, or `make pdf`
from the package root. The article can be built without rerunning the experiments:
its table inputs are included. `tools/render_tables.py` regenerates the tables
from the saved result JSON, rounding interval endpoints outward.

## Package layout

- `article/`: PDF, complete TeX, and table inputs.
- `tools/`: exact verifier, symbolic checks, numerical checks, and table generator.
- `data/`: certificate inputs, three result records, and root asymptotic CSV.
- `corrections/`: a scoped audit and proposed replacement TeX snippets.
- `provenance/`: source identifiers, proof/dependency map, environment and validation record.
- `SHA256SUMS`: hashes of the deliverable files, excluding itself.

The suggested integration is a new self-contained subdirectory, for example
`Analysis/Polylogarithms/research/stieltjes_zero_geometry/`. Keeping `tools/`

# Color-Coded Affine Partitions

**Exact Boundary Saturation and a Two-Term Growth Law**  
Research manuscript prepared for the ProveIt project — October 7, 2026.

## Main result

Let `C_{s,q}` be the union of the `s` coordinate lines in `F_q^s`, and let `P_{s,n}(q)` be the minimum number of whole-field affine cells in a disjoint partition of `C_{s,q}^n`. For each fixed prime power `q > 2`, put `t = q-1` and `gamma_q = log(t)/log(1+1/t)`. The manuscript proves

```text
rho_s(q) = lim_{n -> infinity} P_{s,n}(q)^(1/n)
         = t*s - gamma_q + O_{q,epsilon}(s^(-1+epsilon))
```

for every positive epsilon. The positive error after the two displayed terms has logarithmic exponent `-1`. A sharper explicit upper error is `C_q*(K_s+3)/s`, where `log K_s ~ log s/log log s` and `K_s` is defined by integer factorial and perfect-hash bounds in the article.

The construction exactly attains

```text
P_{s,m}(q) = t*(s*t)^m - (t-1)*(1+s*t)^m
```

whenever `m/s + binom(m,2)/s^2 <= 1`, and in a substantially larger region certified by the color-coded residue budget. The endpoint of exact attainment is within `s^(o(1))` of `t*log(1+1/t)*s`, uniformly in `q > 2`.

Exact examples include `P_{3,2}(q) = 3*q^2-q-1` and `P_{4,3}(q) = 16*q^3-12*q^2-13*q+10`.

a_j=(j+1)\log(j+1)-j\log j-1,\qquad
g_0=1,\qquad g_n=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jg_{n-j},
\]

let \(\rho\in(0,1)\) solve \(\sum a_j\rho^j=1\), and let

\[
g_n=\gamma\rho^{-n}-\frac1{n^2\log^2n}
\left(1+\frac2{\log n}-\frac{\pi^2}{2\log^2n}
-\frac{2\pi^2+8\zeta(3)}{\log^3n}+O(\log^{-4}n)\right).

Throughout, "formal reduction" means reduction in the rational pre-Bloch
group by the standard five-term calculus, with logarithmic products and
rational multiples of pi^2 allowed in the analytic realization. The exact
criterion for a reduced positive rational p/q is

    p^2 == +1 or -1 (mod q), and q^2 == +1 or -1 (mod p).

The signs are independent; the condition modulo 1 is vacuous. Successful
formal reductions give actual dilogarithm identities. A nonzero exterior
symbol rules out a certificate in this calculus; it does not prove that no
accidental numerical relation can exist. No transcendence or numerical
independence statement is inferred from a failed integer-relation search.

The core program computes C(p/q) such that

    F(p/q)-F(1)-C(p/q)

remaining logarithmic expression. All dilogarithm arguments in the produced
core lie strictly between 0 and 1. The consecutive-integer shortcut keeps
the number of terms O(log max(p,q)); optional diagnostic prime factorization
is a separate computation and has no asserted polynomial bit complexity.

conditions stated in the article. Algebraic expansions and exponentially
small displacements are distinguished by defining the reference transition
exactly before subtracting it.

For the elementary harmonic symmetric functions

`e_r(n) = [u^r] product_{j=1}^n (1+u/j)`,

study `T_(p,r)(a) = sum_n (-1)^n e_r(n)/(n+a)^p` and the Gaussian specialization
`S_(p,r) = 2^(-p) T_(p,r)(1/2)`. The manuscript proves:

- An incomplete-beta reflection identity and a finite triangular reduction
  for every harmonic index, with explicit gamma-coefficient recurrences.
- An all-weight formula for the draft's `S_(2m+1,1)`, replacing finite numerical
  evidence by an analytic proof.
- Signed first-omitted-term bounds for every truncation, even before summand
  magnitudes become decreasing, and exact Taylor radii after pole stripping.

  polynomial construction. A separate theorem covers fixed p and growing r.
- A geometrically convergent evaluator with an explicit rational error bound
  in the Gaussian case, implemented using exact rational interval arithmetic.

polylogarithm parity reductions are established in the literature cited in

## Article and status

**Zeros, Distribution Modules, and Regularized Duality in the Stieltjes Parameter-Derivative Tower** is a 24-page, self-contained mathematical article prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt project on 7 October 2026.

The article is `Analysis/Polylogarithms/docs/articles/stieltjes-zeros-distribution-duality.tex`, with the compiled PDF alongside it. Its scope is the generalized-Stieltjes, Hurwitz-jet, and cyclotomic-polylogarithm thread in the supplied drafts, not an exhaustive audit of the entire Polylogarithms directory.

The article supplies ordinary mathematical proofs of a global zero bound, a uniform all-order expansion for large parameter-derivative zeros, an all-denominator formal distribution-rank theorem, its finite-jet extension, and an all-order regularized Dirichlet functional equation. Classical ingredients are attributed. The explicit zero-location results and their positive Lerch deformation are proposed research contributions; exhaustive literature priority has not been established. This AI-assisted research draft has not been independently refereed or verified by a proof assistant. No arithmetic independence theorem is claimed.

## Main results

For every fixed Stieltjes index `n >= 0` and parameter-derivative order `k >= 1`, `gamma_n^(k)(a)` has at most `n` positive zeros, counted with multiplicity. For fixed `n`, all `n` zeros are present and simple for all sufficiently large `k`. These assertions extend to the positive Lerch deformation `0 <= rho <= 1` described in the article, with a large-order threshold uniform in `rho`.

The zeros have complete expansions in descending powers of `k`. Their slopes are the exponentials of negatives of the real roots of reciprocal-gamma Appell polynomials. The first two coefficients are explicit, the next has a directly implementable formula, and an all-order recursion is proved. At `n = 1` there is a unique simple positive zero for every `k`; it lies strictly above `exp(H_(k-1))`, at or below `exp(H_k)`, decreases with `rho`, and moves right with `k`.

The formal distribution quotient has dimension `phi(q)`, and dimension `phi(q)-1` after making the integral coordinate background, for every denominator and every complex weight with positive real part. The jet version is a free module of the same rank. These are dimensions modulo specified relations, not dimensions of spans of actual numerical constants.

The functional equation is normalized after removing the simple trivial zero. This gives the exact `L''(-k)/(2 L'(-k))` first logarithmic derivative and an explicit formula at every higher order.

Copy the `Analysis/Polylogarithms/` subtree into the matching repository directory. All filenames in this bundle are new. No historical article is overwritten and no GitHub commit or pull request is created by this bundle.

make -f Makefile.stieltjes-tower test

lambda(n,r) = M_r(n) p^r - M_(r+1)(n) p^(r+1)

# Beyond Geometric Progressions: Supergeometric Sequences and All Infinite Linear Recurrences

Research manuscript and reproducibility package, dated **8 October 2026**.

The article proves two extensions of finite random routing for the Erdős similarity problem: a finite-block criterion allowing logarithmic gaps to grow without bound, and one common avoiding set for all convergent real constant-coefficient linear recurrences. The second extension, combined with classical bounded-recurrence structure, yields one compact set of arbitrarily large measure avoiding every real linear recurrence with infinite range.

**Status.** This is an AI-assisted research manuscript with complete ordinary mathematical proofs, separate AI audit notes, and finite computational checks. The extensions are new relative to the specific source versions inspected. Worldwide priority is not certified. The manuscript has not been externally refereed, and this package contains no Lean, Rocq, or other proof-assistant formalization. The checks support particular finite mechanisms; they do not certify the infinite theorems.

Suggested ProveIt destination:

```text
Analysis/ErdosSimilarity/Research/supergeometric-and-recurrence-avoidance/
```

## Article and results

The main files are [supergeometric_and_recurrence_avoidance.tex](supergeometric_and_recurrence_avoidance.tex) and the **28-page** [supergeometric_and_recurrence_avoidance.pdf](supergeometric_and_recurrence_avoidance.pdf). The [theorem ledger](THEOREM_LEDGER.md) distinguishes the new core lemmas from inherited constructions, classical facts, and consequences.

### 1. Long finite blocks with growing logarithmic gaps

Let a fixed positive sequence tend to zero. Suppose its values contain decreasing finite blocks

$$
b_{j,1}>\cdots>b_{j,L_j}>0,\qquad L_j\longrightarrow\infty,
$$

with one fixed $0<\mu<1$ such that

$$
b_{j,k+1}\le\mu b_{j,k},\qquad
G_j=\max_{k<L_j}\log\frac{b_{j,k}}{b_{j,k+1}}
=o(\log\log L_j).
$$

For every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there is a closed, symmetric, 1-periodic set $F$, of measure greater than $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval, that omits infinitely many distinct points from every affine copy of the sequence. Its compact section in $[0,1]$ has the same avoidance property. The blocks need not be consecutive in the original sequence; their positions and the gaps between blocks are unrestricted. Here $F$ may depend on the fixed sequence.

A sufficient prefix condition for a positive decreasing sequence with $a_{n+1}\le\mu a_n$ eventually is

$$
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{G_N}{\log\log N}=0,
\qquad G_N=\max_{n_0\le j<N}\log\frac{a_j}{a_{j+1}}.
$$

The simpler pointwise condition $\log(a_n/a_{n+1})=o(\log\log n)$ implies this criterion. Examples include

$$
a_n=\exp[-n(\log\log n)^\gamma],\quad 0<\gamma<1,
\qquad
a_n=\exp[-n\log\log\log n],
$$

after a fixed initial index shift. Their adjacent ratios tend to zero. The article also gives a completely rational example and an example showing that the local block criterion is stronger than the prefix test.

The new budget argument chooses the branching number from the available block length and proves that the entire construction fits inside that block. Its required span satisfies

$$
\log\sigma_d=O_{p,\mu}\bigl(\sqrt{\log L}\,\log\log\log L\bigr)=o(\log L).
$$

The quantitative appendix gives a sharper sufficient normalized-scale budget, $\log\log L\ge G/p+C G^{3/4}$, with blocker density at most $p+5\tau$ for fixed $p,\tau,\mu$. This refinement does not establish a positive-constant replacement for the zero limit in the all-scale criterion.

### 2. One set for all convergent real linear recurrences

For every $0<\varepsilon<1$, one closed, symmetric, 1-periodic set $F_{\mathrm{rec},\varepsilon}$, of measure greater than $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval, simultaneously omits infinitely many distinct points from every affine copy of every convergent real homogeneous constant-coefficient linear recurrence that is not eventually constant.

The set is independent of the recurrence order, coefficients, roots, initial state, translation, and nonzero scale. The proof permits nonreal contracting roots, repeated or colliding roots, exact zero terms, signs, and cancellations. A first crossing of the norm of a consecutive state block supplies separated nonzero scalar samples. Polynomial sign conditions, including zero signs, count the possible routing addresses. Rational compact families of stable companion matrices cover all stable tails without a uniform separation assumption on eigenvalues.

For rational $\varepsilon$, the construction can be made effectively closed with computable Lebesgue measure. The existence proof gives a terminating search using real quantifier elimination; the supplied Python scripts do not implement that search. No practical complexity bound or computable distance function is claimed.

### 3. All infinite-range recurrences, classification, and matrix orbits

The compact section $K=F_{\mathrm{rec},\varepsilon}\cap[0,1]$ is nowhere dense and satisfies

$$
\#\bigl(\{x+sa_n:n\ge0\}\setminus K\bigr)=\infty
$$

for every real constant-coefficient recurrence with infinite range, every $x\in\mathbb R$, and every $s\ne0$. This conclusion has no convergence, boundedness, or spectral restriction. The reduction uses the classical fact that bounded recurrence sequences split into finitely many arithmetic subsequences with compact interval sets of tail limits; the needed bounded case is proved in full.

Consequently, within real constant-coefficient recurrences, the value set is measure universal **if and only if it is finite**, equivalently if and only if the sequence is eventually periodic. A product construction gives the corresponding statement for every infinite image of a finite-dimensional real matrix orbit. A countable prescribed collection of sequences from result 1 can also be avoided together with all infinite-range recurrences by one compact set.

## Scope boundaries

- The general Erdős similarity conjecture is not resolved. The displayed hypotheses do not cover $e^{-n^2}$ or $1/n!$, and the article makes no global literature-status claim about those examples.
- The finite-block theorem uses a maximum logarithmic gap, not an average-gap hypothesis. Its uniform upper ratio $\mu<1$ remains an assumption.
- The supergeometric avoiding set is sequence-dependent. The package does not claim one set for the uncountable class of all arbitrary sequences satisfying that criterion.
- The unrestricted recurrence theorem concerns compact $K$. A nonempty 1-periodic $F$ contains $x+\mathbb Z$ for each $x\in F$ and therefore cannot avoid every unbounded recurrence.
- Finite patterns are measure universal. Infinite range, or non-eventual constancy in the convergent version, is a necessary exclusion.
- In the matrix-orbit consequence, the transformed image must be infinite. A nonzero linear map can annihilate an orbit.
